Sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons relative to full-catalog evaluation; fixed negatives improve comparability but do not remove sampling bias ([Krichene & Rendle, 2020](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)). Preserve the host’s users, 99 negatives, seeds and HR@10 calculation; interpret results specifically under that protocol. Applying [paired bootstrap resampling](https://aclanthology.org/W04-3250/) here: retain each model’s per-user hit indicator, resample 200 users with replacement within each category using identical sampled indices for both models, then average the four category differences equally. Report the observed macro HR@10 difference and a bootstrap 95% interval. This estimates user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates; it excludes training randomness and candidate-resampling uncertainty. If per-user results are unavailable, aggregate HR alone cannot recover paired uncertainty.

Repeated hyperparameter and checkpoint selection can overfit a small validation panel: maximizing a noisy criterion introduces selection bias ([Cawley & Talbot, 2010](https://www.jmlr.org/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)); adaptive holdout reuse compounds the problem ([Dwork et al., 2015](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper/2015/hash/bad5f33780c42f2588878a9d07405083-Abstract.html)). Practical safeguards inferred for this constrained search: predeclare the search budget, evaluation cadence, meaningful improvement threshold and tie-breaking rule; log every evaluated configuration and checkpoint; avoid expanding search around tiny gains. Treat bootstrap intervals after selection as descriptive, not selection-adjusted significance guarantees. Keep selection on the mandated macro validation HR@10, flag uncertain gains, and reserve held-out test evaluation for the final selected model. Bootstrap diagnostics require no retraining or evaluator changes.
